projects.line: Make room for a calmer first step.
projects.description: An experience design study connecting a gentle introduction, meditation content, practitioner discovery, and a personal wellbeing overview.

domains.title: Personal finance — making information actionable
domains.text: A balance, a spending total, and an investment valuation can look similar on a dashboard while answering different questions. My interest is in helping someone understand what a figure means, which period it describes, and what decision it can support. BeeRich explores that relationship between financial information and a useful next step.
domains.question: What can someone understand or decide after seeing this?
domains.name: BeeRich

domains.title: Merchant operations — designing around the moment
domains.text: Merchant software sits inside work that is already happening: a table changes status, an order needs attention, or a payment is waiting for confirmation. I look at what the person needs to know at that moment and which action should be easiest to find. mSeller brings workflow analysis and interface hierarchy into the same conversation.
domains.question: What should be obvious when attention is limited?
domains.name: mSeller

domains.title: Debt and payment records — making change traceable
domains.text: A remaining balance is the result of events. Understanding those events matters when a payment is partial, repeated, unmatched, or corrected. Debt Ledger is where my interest in journey mapping meets business-rule thinking: the visible amount should have an explanation that the product can consistently support.
domains.question: Can we explain why the record changed?
domains.name: Debt Ledger

domains.title: Digital wellbeing — making the first step approachable
domains.text: A wellbeing experience asks someone to give attention to themselves. I want that beginning to feel understandable and voluntary. Moodify explores how introductory guidance, self-guided content, and the option to connect with another person might sit together without making the experience feel demanding.
domains.question: How can the experience offer direction while preserving choice?
domains.name: Moodify

steps.title: Understand the moment
steps.description: Identify the task, the context, and what is difficult about the current experience.
steps.question: In mSeller, what does the staff member need to do while serving an order?

steps.title: Name the decision
steps.description: Make clear what the user and the business need to decide.
steps.question: In BeeRich, which financial question should the overview help answer first?

steps.title: Make the rules visible
steps.description: Connect the screen to the conditions and events that govern its behavior.
steps.question: In Debt Ledger, what evidence allows a payment to change the balance?

steps.title: Compare the alternatives
steps.description: Explore more than one direction and explain the cost of each choice.
steps.question: In Moodify, how much onboarding is useful before someone can explore?

steps.title: Design for the exception
steps.description: Include uncertainty, interruption, and recovery in the experience.
steps.question: What should happen when a request is sent but confirmation is still pending?

steps.title: Define what to learn
steps.description: Choose evidence that can test whether the experience is useful.
steps.question: Can someone complete the task and explain what happened without assistance?

personal: I like moving between the larger product question and the small interaction that makes it real. This portfolio brings together selected work and reflections on those decisions.
